Action Plan:
1. Provide supportive care for acute diarrhoea: soft diet (toast, crackers, jam, mashed vegetables), avoid dairy/meat/eggs/fish until 48 h symptom-free; yogurt permitted for probiotic benefit.  
2. Encourage oral hydration; purchase over-the-counter Dioralyte to replace lost electrolytes.  
3. Safety-net advice: seek review if (a) motions increase to ≥6–8/day, (b) diarrhoea lasts >7 days, or (c) any blood appears in stool—stool sample and/or hospital assessment may then be required.  
4. Written summary placed in patient’s app for later reference.  
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of “bad diarrhoea.”  
• History of presenting illness:  
  – 4–5 loose/watery stools per day; variable consistency.  
  – Mild abdominal pain.  
  – One episode of vomiting.  
  – Possible low-grade fever (not measured).  
  – Reduced appetite.  
  – Denies blood or mucus in stool.  
  – No recent travel; no suspicious food intake.  
  – Able to maintain oral fluids.  
  – No medications taken for symptoms yet.  
• Past medical history: asthma.  
• Surgical history: none mentioned.  
• Medications: inhaler named “Lexapro” (dose/route/frequency not documented; exact product uncertain).  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Family history: father hypertensive, died of bowel cancer at age 62.  
• Social history: not discussed (smoking, alcohol, occupation not documented).

Objective:
• General appearance via video: patient appears well hydrated.  
• No vitals or physical examination findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis (DDx: “Acute viral gastroenteritis” – High likelihood).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis – Medium (no obvious food risk but possible).  
     • Medication-induced diarrhoea (if “Lexapro” is escitalopram) – Low-Medium.  
     • IBS-D – Low (lack of chronic pattern).  
     • IBD flare – Low (no blood/mucus; very short course).  
   – Investigations planned: None initially; stool culture if symptoms >1 week or blood appears.  
   – Treatment planned: Dietary modification (soft diet, yogurt), oral rehydration (Dioralyte), maintain fluids.  
   – Safety-net: Return if ≥6–8 motions/day, persisting >7 days, blood in stool, or signs of dehydration.

2. Asthma medication clarification  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stable asthma; inhaler brand/name uncertain.  
   – Differential diagnosis: n/a.  
   – Investigations planned: None today.  
   – Treatment planned: Clinician to verify inhaler (“Lexapro”) identity at next contact; no change today.  
   – Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: vitals, full physical examination, detailed medication reconciliation (inhaler specifics), social history (smoking/alcohol), immunisation status.  
● No direct conflicts between transcript and DDx noted.  
● Transcript clear; occasional audio repetitions but information intelligible.
